questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles user-controlled values in SQL? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
The sort field comes from the query string and ORDER BY cannot use bound parameters. How does the code keep it safe?
choices: It escapes the value with PDO::quote().
It strips non-alphanumeric characters from the value.
It looks the value up as a key in the SORTABLE map and uses only the mapped column; unknown keys throw.
It relies on ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES being false.

questions.prompt: The status filter builds placeholders :status0, :status1, ... in a loop. Is attacker-supplied text able to change the structure of the SQL here?
choices: No. The number of placeholders depends only on how many values were sent; the values themselves are bound separately.
Yes, because the status strings are used to name the placeholders.
Yes, but only when more than one status is sent.
No, but only because the values are validated against an enum first.

questions.prompt: A user searches for the text 50%_off. What does escapeLike plus ESCAPE '!' accomplish beyond parameter binding?
choices: It prevents SQL injection, which binding alone would not.
It encodes the text so it is safe to place in the JSON response.
It makes % and _ in the input match literally instead of acting as LIKE wildcards.
